newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-Indian GDRs surge amid budget euphoria.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-Indian GDRs surge amid budget euphoria.

text.p: Indian global depositary recepits (GDRs) surged in London trading after the country's finance minister sparked jubilation with a 1997-98 budget that traders described as a gift to the market.

"It was just a tremendous budget for the market -- local traders are euphoric, they are talking of the market going up 1,000 points," said one dealer at a major brokerage here. "It will definitely go to 3,800 on Monday and GDRs will follow."

Indian GDRs shot up 6.07 percent, or 4.14 points, to 72.39 on the HSBC james Capel GDR index after Finance Minister P. Chidambaram announced a bold package of measures that spelt a giant leap forward for the country's process of economic reform.

The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index soared 5.13 percent, or 178.20 points, to 3,652.99 in a special post-budget trading session, while the premium for GDRs over the local market climbed to 14.82 percent.
Traders said the market was particularly cheered by huge cuts in income and corporate tax rates and in import duties, as well as by measures allowing companies to buy back their own shares.
The budget also took steps to widen the tax net and encourage investment.
"The market loves it," said one dealer, adding the market saw the budget as particularly beneficial for the consumer sector.
While consumer stocks are not well represented on the GDR market, it does represent most of India's blue chip stocks and would continue to benefit as trading continues next week, he said.
GDRs in India's largest private firm, Reliance Industries Ltd, climbed 1.80 percent to $17.05 due in part to the reduction in the minimum alternate tax (MAT) rate to 10.5 percent from 12.9.
One dealer said U.S. investors had yet to fully participate in the euphoria, and that this should drive the market to higher levels next week.

Elsewhere, Korean shares ended the day higher on rumours that an announcement of a rise in the foreign shareholders' ceiling was imminent. The ceiling is expected to be lifted to 23 percent from 20 percent some time this year, but no date has been set for the change.
The Capel Korea GDR Index, however, ended 0.13 points, or 0.22 percent, lower at 58.09, with the premium over the local market at 34.61 percent.
The Korea Composite Index rose 7.12 points to 676.53.
Taiwan stocks also ended higher, with the weighted index fighting off late profit-taking to end up 0.55 percent at 7,875.32.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended up 0.50 points, or 0.49 percent at 103.09, with a premium of 1.04 percent over the local market. -- Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 5887
